summary: This sermon introduces Sabbath as a spiritual practice woven into creation from Genesis, designed to counter our culture's busyness and productivity obsession. The pastor argues that Sabbath is not an outdated Old Testament rule but an ongoing invitation from God to stop working, rest, delight, and worship, reminding us that our value comes from being God's image-bearers rather than what we produce or consume.
key_points: Sabbath is a rhythm built into the fabric of creation itself
It's a counter-formational practice against cultural pressures of productivity and FOMO
The Sabbath command calls us to remember our identity as image-bearers, not slaves
Practical invitation to work toward a weekly 24-hour period of rest, delight, and worship
Sabbath is a foretaste of eternal rest in new creation
big_idea: Sabbath is God's invitation woven into creation for us to stop producing and find our identity not in what we do but in being His image-bearers, offering both personal soul-rest and counter-cultural witness in an anxious, overworked society.
title: PTW Sabbath: STOP
